title: The article discusses the recent Commonwealth Summit in Vancouver, highlighting Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher's perceived role and the ongoing unofficial dealings between African states and South Africa. It notes that Thatcher's stance may shift her image from villain to savior, especially in light of Canada's generous debt write-off for African nations. The piece also touches on the tensions between Canada and Britain regarding trade with South Africa, and South African Foreign Minister Pik Botha's criticisms of Commonwealth countries, particularly Canada and Australia, for their human rights records. Additionally, it mentions Mozambique's interest in joining the Commonwealth and the complex relationships between Commonwealth and France-African summit members.
